  1                 I. PRELIMINARY STATEMENT REGARDING TESTIMONY

 2   Q. Please describe the nature of your testimony.

 3   A. I submit this testimony as a landowner pro se intervenor with personal knowledge of
 4   my property and the conditions that would be directly affected by the proposed 765 kV
 5   transmission line.

 6   My testimony is based on my work experiences, personal observations, firsthand
 7   knowledge, and direct experience regarding my property, including its use,
 8   infrastructure, and planned future residential and agricultural use.

 9   To the extent I offer opinions, those opinions are rationally based on my firsthand
10   knowledge and are offered as permissible lay opinion testimony under Texas Rule of
11   Evidence 701.

12   To the extent I reference publicly available studies, agency reports, legislative materials,
13   scientific literature, or statements by others, those references are offered solely to
14   explain the basis of my concerns and understanding of potential impacts. With this
15   direct testimony I am not offering expert testimony under Texas Rule of Evidence 702.

16   My testimony is relevant under Texas Rules of Evidence 401 and 402 because it
17   addresses direct impacts to my property.

18

19                                II. PERSONAL INFORMATION:

20   Q. Please state your name and address.

21   A. My name is Christopher Landgraf. My impacted property address is 505 County

22   Road 322, Bartlett, TX 76511. I own the impacted property with my wife, Merriam

23   Mukai-Agha. My current homestead address is 1605 Dubiel Drive, Leander, TX 78641.

24   Q. Are you the same Christopher Landgraf who filed a Motion to Intervene in this

25   proceeding?




                                                             Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                        SOAH Docket
                                                                                   No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 5 of 28
  1   A. Yes. PUC Docket Number 59475, Link E3, Track 2682, Request to Intervene by

 2   Interchange Filing Item 168 and granted by Item 396 (SOAH Order No. 3).

 3   Q. Please state your background.

 4   A. My name is Christopher Landgraf. I am a registered Professional Engineer in the

 5   State of Texas (License No. 107480). I am a member of the Association for Materials

 6   Protection and Performance (AMPP, Member No. 11591296). In 2002, I received a

 7   Bachelor of Science degree in chemical engineering from the University of Texas at

 8   Austin. I am employed as an Engineer IV at Texas Gas Service (TGS), a Division of

 9   ONE Gas in Austin, Texas, where I have worked for over 21 years. TGS owns and

10   operates natural gas distribution and transmission facilities in the Austin, Texas area

11   and is a regulated natural gas utility. As an engineer at TGS, I have been involved with

12   projects that bring new natural gas supplies to the TGS Austin system and supply

13   natural gas to a variety of customers (up to and including power plants). My projects

14   have involved route planning (sometimes involving condemnation), system modeling,

15   preventative and reactive induced voltage/current mitigation, and installations to limit

16   step and touch potentials.

17   Q. Are you testifying on behalf of the above-listed landowner?

18   A. Yes.

19   Q. Is the property affected by the transmission line project proposed by Oncor

20   Electric Delivery Company LLC?


                                                             Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                        SOAH Docket
                                                                                   No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 6 of 28
  1   A. Yes.

 2   Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?

 3   A. The purpose of my testimony is to help parties involved in this process make a

 4   thoughtful and informed decision on the proposed 765 kV transmission line.

 5   Q. What are the routes on this property?

 6   A. Routes containing Link E3. From the complete list of 1,246 alternative routes, Link E3

 7   appears in routes 305-382, 874-889, 910-949, 990-1012, 1083-1089, 1115-1125, 1156-

 8   1165, and 1168-1175. From the 122 alternative routes filed with the CCN Application,

 9   Link E3 appears in routes 322, 366, 376, 381, 382, 910, 911, 913-916, 1162, and 1164.

10   Q. What routes do you oppose?

11   A. I oppose routes containing Links E3, E4, and F41. Alternative routes containing Link

12   E3 are listed in my previous response. From the complete list of 1,246 alternative

13   routes, Link E4 appears in routes 328-342, 367-382, 883-889, and 999-1005 and Link

14   F41 appears in routes 305-327, 343-366, 874-882, 910-949, 990-998, 1006-1012,

15   1083-1089, 1115-1125, 1156-1165, 1168-1175. From the 122 alternative routes filed

16   with the CCN Application, Link E4 appears in routes 376, 381, and 382 and Link F41

17   appears in routes 322, 366, 910, 911, 913-916, 1162, and 1164.

18   Q. What routes do you support?

19   A. I do not support the proposed project overall. With the assumption that the project

20   was to continue, alternative route 894 is what I support.
                                                            Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                       SOAH Docket
                                                                                  No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 7 of 28
  1   Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?

 2   A. No.

 3   Q. Was this material prepared by you or under your supervision?

 4   A. Yes.

 5                               DESCRIPTION AND LOCATION

 6   Q. Do you have pictures that depict the property and how it is used?

 7   A. Exhibit A shows the overall approximate 25.14-acre parcel (identified as Parcel #

 8   2682) and Exhibit B is a Google Street View image of the northeast corner of the parcel

 9   from County Road 322. The majority of the property is currently leased for hay

10   production with exception of the northeast corner which is currently used as storage.

11   Q. Have the pictures been altered?

12   A. Exhibit A was sourced/screenshot from the LCRA Bell County East to Big Hill

13   Primary Route Segments Map GIS viewer and Exhibit B was sourced/screenshot from

14   Google Street View using Google Maps. Neither of the pictures were altered by me.

15   Q. Do the pictures accurately represent the views of the property?

16   A. Overall, yes. Note that the green property boundaries shown in Exhibit A appear to

17   be shifted/off by approximately 45 feet; I had the property perimeter staked by a

18   surveyor at the time of property purchase and had the 30 foot by 30 foot metal building

19   installed within the property perimeter (contrary to what’s shown by Exhibit A).

                                                            Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                       SOAH Docket
                                                                                  No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 8 of 28
  1   Q. Description of the property?

 2   A. The property is approximately 25.14 acres and triangular in shape. The property has

 3   historically been used in agricultural production.

 4   Q. Approximately where is your location in the study area?

 5   A. Please see Exhibit A. The property is designated as Parcel 2682 with Link E3

 6   essentially going through the middle of the property and splitting it into approximately

 7   equal halves (by area). Optional Links E4 and F41 are located just to the west of the

 8   property.

 9                           LAND USE, CONCERNS AND HISTORY

10   Q. Please give a brief history of the property and your association with it.

11   A. My wife and I were interested in purchasing the property in early 2021 but our plans

12   were delayed as I got busy with work helping prepare for and operate through Winter

13   Storm Uri; we ended up closing on the property April 7, 2021. We purchased the

14   property with the intention of moving to it and making it our homestead. We had Barlett

15   Electric Cooperative install a service lateral for a 320-amp delivery in 2021 with the

16   intent of using it for our homestead and future homesite. In 2022, we installed a 30 foot

17   by 30 foot metal building, had it spray foamed, added electrical to it, and installed a

18   mini-split HVAC system to it in 2023. After getting busy with work and life in 2024, we

19   were preparing to continue on with plans for our envisioned barndominium install when




                                                             Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                        SOAH Docket
                                                                                   No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 9 of 28
  1   we received notice from Oncor/LCRA about the proposed project in the summer of

 2   2025.

 3   Q. Please describe how the property is used today and how this transmission line

 4   may affect that use.

 5   A. As mentioned earlier, the property is currently primarily leased out for hay production

 6   with some it currently being used for storage. While we had intention of continuing to

 7   turn the property into our homestead, those plans were immediately put on hold when

 8   we found out about the Oncor/LCRA project as we have no intention of living near

 9   higher voltage power lines.

10   Q. What types of concerns do you have with regard to the transmission line

11   segments and routes proposed?

12   A. My wife originally purchased an EMF meter in 2018 when we initially started looking

13   for a future homestead location to ensure whatever property we purchased didn’t have

14   elevated EMF levels as we had concerns about some of the publicly available

15   information we had seen regarding elevated EMF levels (please see Exhibits H and I).

16   Further compounding concerns for me is that fact that my uncle died of Leukemia and

17   lived near a higher voltage line in Dallas County, Texas. Based on my observations

18   using the EMF meter around lesser voltage power lines in the area, I have concerns

19   regarding the potential EMF levels that we’d likely see at our property if Links E3, E4,

20   and/or F41 were constructed. Additionally, based on my personal knowledge and

21   experience working as an engineer at TGS, I have significant concerns about the

                                                            Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                       SOAH Docket
                                                                                  No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                       Page 10 of 28
  1   hazards associated with induced voltage/current if Links E3, E4 and/or F41 were

 2   constructed on/near my property.

 3   Q. Of the 122 alternative routes filed with the CCN Application, how do routes

 4   containing Link E3 compare to routes that don’t contain Link E3?

 5   A. There’s a popular saying that the shortest distance between two points is a straight

 6   line. Related to this project, that would be a proposed route that goes as straight as

 7   possible from East Bell to Big Hill. Given that Link E3 is fairly far south of East Bell and

 8   that East Bell and Big Hill are roughly east/west of each other, the 13 routes that make

 9   use of Link E3 are in the top 15 of 122 route combinations for the longest and costliest

10   routes (using applicant’s native Table 2 File, Environmental Data for Alternative Filed

11   Routes in the CCN Application (Feet), as a basis for assessment). Based on my

12   personal knowledge and experience, longer routes will usually cost more (generally

13   engineering, easement, material, construction labor, etc costs trend with route length).

14   Additionally, given the longer route distances for combinations including Link E3, it’s not

15   surprising that the 13 routes containing Link E3 on average contain more habitable

16   structures within 500 feet. Following the logic of the CCN application assessment, it’s

17   my understanding that SOAH and PUC should choose a route that doesn’t contain Link

18   E3. See Exhibit C for calculations/analysis. Note that of the 122 alternate routes filed

19   with the CCN application, Links E4 or F41 only appear as route options when Link E3 is

20   also chosen.

21                                       FINANCIAL RISKS

                                                              Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                               PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                         SOAH Docket
                                                                                    No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 11 of 28
  1   Q. What do you think the financial risks will be to you?

 2   A. I have no desire to live next to higher voltage power lines so we would likely attempt

 3   to sell the property if Links E3, E4 and/or F41 were to be constructed and would attempt

 4   to get compensated for easement take and/or damages but I have significant concerns

 5   that compensation may not fully cover devaluation.

 6   Q. What are the risks of devaluation of your property?

 7   A. Based on my personal knowledge and experience, Link E3 is likely to devalue my

 8   property as it would take 200 foot wide easement essentially through the middle of my

 9   property and lessen what could potentially be done with the property in the future.

10   Additionally, based on my personal knowledge and experience, Links E4 and F41 are

11   also likely to devalue my property even though the easement take wouldn’t be on my

12   property. Please see Exhibit G.

13   Q. Does Link E3 run along the edge of other properties that it crosses?

14   A. Please see Exhibit D. Of the 16 parcels that Link E3 is proposed to encroach upon,

15   only on 1 of the parcels (Parcel 2687) does the proposed centerline appear to run 100

16   foot off of an existing property line. Based on my personal knowledge and experience, I

17   suspect additional cost and damage beyond the 200’ easement take because of how 15

18   of the 16 properties are being crossed.

19   Q. How does Link E3 interact with the proposed Williamson County Ronald

20   Reagan Extension from IH-35 to SH-95?


                                                            Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                       SOAH Docket
                                                                                  No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                       Page 12 of 28
  1   A. During the June 17, 2025, Lampasas Public Participation Meeting, I pointed out via

 2   the questionnaire/feedback paperwork that Williamson County was proposing to extend

 3   Ronald Reagan from IH-35 to SH-95 (see Exhibit E for information on that project) and

 4   that the same consultant working on the Oncor/LCRA project (Halff) had worked on the

 5   Williamson County project. Additionally, I mentioned how I had seen LCRA install

 6   higher voltage poles on/along/parallel to another section of Ronald Reagan closer to my

 7   current homestead (see Exhibit F). I was hoping that the Oncor/LCRA project might be

 8   able to somewhat plan ROW/easement takes with the Williamson County project to

 9   lessen property impacts in the area (with the understanding that the currently proposed

10   project towers have a larger footprint) but I noticed route E3 wasn’t updated from its

11   preliminary routing. The proposed ROW and easement takes roughly parallel each

12   other but are substantially offset from each other along E3; I have concern that this will

13   damage my property and the others along E3 more than necessary based on my

14   personal knowledge and experience.

15           HEALTH, SAFETY, ENVIRONMENTAL AND AGRICULTURAL RISKS

16   Q. What do you think are the health risks?

17   A. As stated previously, I have concerns about some of the publicly available

18   information I have seen regarding elevated EMF levels. Based on my observations

19   using our EMF meter around lesser voltage power lines in the area, I have concerns

20   regarding the potential EMF levels that we’d likely see at our property if Links E3, E4,

21   and/or F41 were constructed.

                                                            Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                       SOAH Docket
                                                                                  No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                       Page 13 of 28
  1   Q. What do you see as safety risks?

 2   A. As stated previously, based on my personal knowledge and experience working as

 3   an engineer at TGS, I have significant concerns about the hazards associated with

 4   induced voltage/current if Links E3, E4 and/or F41 were constructed on/near my

 5   property.

 6   Q. What do you think will be the environmental impacts and risks?

 7   A. The darker colored vegetation running roughly north and south within the middle of

 8   my property (see Exhibit A) is a wet weather creek. During more intense rain events, I

 9   have observed a substantial amount of surface water flow going towards the wet

10   weather creek so I have significant concerns about erosion and soil loss that could

11   occur given construction activity associated with Link E3 (based on my personal

12   knowledge and experience).

13   Q. What do you think will be the risks to your agricultural activities and animals?

14   A. We had intent to raise animals on the property once it became our homestead. I

15   have significant concerns regarding possible fencing that we might put up for the

16   animals and possible risks associated with induced voltage getting onto the fencing if

17   Links E3, E4, and/or F41 were installed.

18                 RECREATION, COMMUNITY VALUES AND AESTHETICS

19   Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?



                                                           Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                      SOAH Docket
                                                                                 No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 14 of 28
  1   A. The health and safety concerns that I previously mentioned would always be in the

 2   back of my head and would adversely impact my enjoyment of the property.

 3   Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use

 4   on your land?

 5   A. Yes. As previously stated, we intended for the property to be our homestead and

 6   we’d likely not continue with those plans if Links E3, E4 and/or F41 were constructed.

 7   Q. How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your

 8   area?

 9   A. I have attended numerous meetings in the area regarding the proposed Oncor/LCRA

10   project and have been impressed with the turnout of neighbors that I’ve historically had

11   limited interaction with (coming together unlike what I’m accustomed to living within city

12   limits). I’ve observed many people at the meetings and in the comments on the PUC

13   Interchange state that they plan to relocate if the proposed Oncor/LCRA lines are built

14   near them. I see ‘destruction’ of close-knit communities as a negative to rural

15   community values.

16   Q. How will this transmission line affect the aesthetic value of your property?

17   A. I like the open field/big sky feel that my property currently has (that’s one of the

18   reasons why we purchased this specific property). If Link combinations E3 & E4 or E4

19   & F41 were chosen, I’d have one of the just-under-200-foot-tall towers just to the west

20   of my property while Link E3 would at least result in conductors crossing my property


                                                              Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                               PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                         SOAH Docket
                                                                                    No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 15 of 28
  1   between towers. All of these Link options would greatly lessen the perceived aesthetic

 2   value I have of the property.

 3   Q. Do transmission routes parallel any existing rights of way on your property?

 4   A. No.

 5   Q. Does Oncor’s application properly identify the structures on your property?

 6   A. While my 30 foot by 30 foot metal building is not habitable from a tax appraisal

 7   perspective, as previously mentioned, I have insulated, added electrical, and installed a

 8   mini-split HVAC to the building. Additionally, I have previously purchased a portable

 9   camping toilet and bottled water dispensing pump system and located an old

10   refrigerator to the building. As I’ve added components to the building which would allow

11   me to live there short term, I believe the argument could be made that the building could

12   have been considered habitable from a route assessment perspective. My 30 foot by

13   30 foot metal building was not identified as a habitable structure in the application.

14                       LOCAL ELECTRICITY SERVICE AND COSTS.

15   Q. Do you think that this transmission line will improve your electric service in

16   your area?

17   A. No. It is my understanding this project (and associated sister projects) are being

18   constructed as part of the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (so that power can flow from

19   east to west).

20   Q. Do you think this transmission line will lower your electricity costs?
                                                             Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                        SOAH Docket
                                                                                   No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 16 of 28
  1   A. Based on the application information, it is my understanding that this project is

 2   estimated to cost just shy of $2 billion. Based on my personal knowledge and

 3   experience, regarding rates for regulated utilities, capital expenditure costs are typically

 4   recovered in rate cases. So, it is my understanding/assumption that this project will

 5   raise electricity costs.

 6   Q. Do you think it’s possible that a better value/more cost-effective solution

 7   exists than the currently proposed project and related sister Permian Basin

 8   Reliability Plan projects?

 9   A. Yes. Watching the April 1, 2026, Senate Committee on Business and Commerce

10   meeting (3:29:05 to end -

11   https://senate.texas.gov/videoplayer.php?vid=22651&lang=en) with ERCOT CEO &

12   PUC chairman and seeing PUC interchange filing Item 3665

13   (https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59475_3665_1638691.PDF)

14   representative/senator letter to PUC commissioners has me thinking/hoping that

15   legislative changes to improve opportunity/chances for dispatchable energy generation

16   (such as natural gas) in the Permian Basin area might be possible. Based on my

17   personal knowledge and experience, pricing for natural gas at the Waha gas hub in the

18   Permian Basin area has been (recent past) and continues to be negative. Addition of

19   new natural gas dispatchable energy generation in the Permian Basin area where the

20   fuel source has a history of being negative in price appear to be ingredients to be able

21   to meet increased electrical demand load in the Permian Basin area versus building out


                                                             Direct Testimony of Christopher Landgraf
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                        SOAH Docket
                                                                                   No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 17 of 28
  1   the 3-path electrical transmission lines as part of the Permian Basin Reliability Plan

 2   solution.

 3                         CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

 4   Q: Is there anything else you would like to have considered in this proceeding?

 5   A. No. In conclusion, I’m wishful in hoping that the entire project doesn’t happen. I’m

 6   hopeful that SOAH and PUC ultimately choose a route that doesn’t contain Link E3

 7   because of its impacts to my specific property, the fact that it’s in the top 15 of 122

 8   alternative routes filed with the CCN Application in length & costs, higher than average

 9   number of habitable structures within 500’, and because of how many E3 parcels are

10   crossed by the Link away from the parcel perimeters. In the event that a route

11   containing Link E3 is ultimately chosen, I’m wishful that an alignment more closely

12   paralleling the proposed Ronald Reagan extension could be chosen (as to lessen

13   combined impacts to E3 properties, including mine).

14   Q. Does this conclude your testimony?

15   A. Yes
